changes.before: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in August indicates that economic growth remains slow.
changes.after: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that economic growth strengthened somewhat in the third quarter, reflecting in part a reversal of the temporary factors that had weighed on growth earlier in the year.

changes.before: Household spending has been increasing at only a modest pace in recent months despite some recovery in sales of motor vehicles as supply-chain disruptions eased.
changes.after: Household spending has increased at a somewhat faster pace in recent months.

changes.before: The Committee continues to expect some pickup in the pace of recovery over coming quarters but anticipates
changes.after: The Committee continues to expect a moderate pace of economic growth over coming quarters and consequently anticipates

changes.before: the Committee decided today to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities.
changes.after: the Committee decided today to continue its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities as announced in September.

changes.before: The Committee discussed the range of policy tools available to promote a stronger economic recovery in a context of price stability.
Voting against the action were Richard W. Fisher, Narayana Kocherlakota, and Charles I. Plosser, who did not support additional policy accommodation at this time.
changes.after: Voting against the action was Charles L. Evans, who supported additional policy accommodation at this time.

parsed.rationale: The statement upgrades its assessment of growth and household spending, drops the reference to discussing the range of available policy tools, and adds no new easing, which modestly lowers the odds of near-term further accommodation. The dissent shifting to a lone dove partly offsets this, but policy settings and forward guidance are unchanged.

spans.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in August indicates that economic growth remains slow.
Household spending has been increasing at only a modest pace in recent months despite some recovery in sales of motor vehicles as supply-chain disruptions eased.
The Committee continues to expect some pickup in the pace of recovery over coming quarters but anticipates
the Committee decided today to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities.
The Committee discussed the range of policy tools available to promote a stronger economic recovery in a context of price stability.
Voting against the action were Richard W. Fisher, Narayana Kocherlakota, and Charles I. Plosser, who did not support additional policy accommodation at this time.

Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that economic growth strengthened somewhat in the third quarter, reflecting in part a reversal of the temporary factors that had weighed on growth earlier in the year.
Household spending has increased at a somewhat faster pace in recent months.
The Committee continues to expect a moderate pace of economic growth over coming quarters and consequently anticipates
the Committee decided today to continue its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities as announced in September.
Voting against the action was Charles L. Evans, who supported additional policy accommodation at this time.
